typedBody.acceptance: The local API maintains validated, persistent inventory, implements the agreed queries and retains every successful concurrent decrement.
typedBody.story: Maintain one household's pantry through a canonical SQLite inventory and JSON API.

typedBody.contract: Provides inventory-query-semantics through GET /api/items under http-api.
typedBody.design: Use the household computer's local date, inclusive expiry bounds, literal Python str.casefold() substring search, intersected filters and deterministic expiry/id ordering.
typedBody.obligation: GET /api/items (optional ?expiring_within=DAYS, ?q=TEXT name search) returns items sorted by expiry (nulls last). Implement all inventory-query-semantics rules, including expired-item inclusion, null exclusion under expiry filtering, parameter validation and id tie-breaking. Expiring soon uses expiring_within=7.

typedBody.expectedEvidence: API-created records cover yesterday, today, the inclusive expiry-window boundary, beyond it, null expiry and equal-expiry ties. Real GET results prove membership, ordering, casefolded literal search, empty search and filter intersection. Invalid, unknown and repeated query parameters return the agreed error.
typedBody.purpose: Protect inventory-query-semantics against off-by-one windows, SQL wildcard interpretation and unstable ordering, which CRUD checks miss. This is the authoritative backend query evidence handle for interface references; wave checks do not repeat its cases.

gap.correction: Trace the real backend expiry-membership and ordering check for yesterday, today, the inclusive seven-day boundary, beyond-window and null expiry. n019 explicitly proves presentation only, while n020 excludes date-edge cases; neither currently proves this part of the criterion. Reuse backend evidence rather than duplicating it in interface fixtures.
